title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own manuscript. It is p. 214 of a printed CRAS note (t. 292, 1981) by Marcus Wanderley, 'Théorie axiomatique de l'orientation des variétés topologiques à bord'. The note summarises his Montpellier thèse de 3e cycle (1980), which was almost certainly written under Grothendieck. It survives as a tiré à part in cote 93.

Setting (previous page): 𝒱•_{≤N} is the category of topological manifolds with boundary of dimension ≤ N, with open embeddings as morphisms. An orientation theory T = (Ω, δ, ν) consists of three data:
- a contravariant functor Ω on boundaryless manifolds, extended by Ω•(V) = Ω(Int V);
- natural 'Stokes maps' δ_V : Ω•(V) → Ω(∂V);
- a normalisation ν : {±1} ≅ Ω(point).
Axiom (a) (previous page) requires Ω to restrict to a sheaf on each V.

This page continues the axioms.
- (b) Separation: for two sections ω, ω', the coincidence locus {x : ω(x) = ω'(x)} is open and also closed. This is a Hausdorff condition on the étalé space.
- (c) Local isomorphism: δ_V identifies the germs of Ω• along ∂V with Ω_{∂V}. That is, Ω•_V|∂V → Ω_{∂V} is an isomorphism of étalé spaces over ∂V. Condition (i) gives local injectivity near the boundary, (ii) local surjectivity.
- Proposition: for every V, the étalé space Ω_V is a 2-sheeted covering, the orientation double cover.
  - Proof idea: separation gives local constancy (Theorem 2 on the next page).
  - Iterating the Stokes isomorphism on half-spaces gives Ω(R^m) ≅ Ω(R^{m-1}) ≅ … ≅ Ω(pt) ≅ {±1}.
  - Hence μ₂ acts on Ω, and −ω denotes the opposite orientation.
- (d) Anti-commutativity: if a boundaryless V is cut along a codimension-1 interface into V' ∪ V'' with V' ∩ V'' = ∂V' = ∂V'', the two induced boundary orientations of a global ω are opposite. This is the usual 'outward normal' sign convention, axiomatised.

Morphisms of theories are natural transformations Ω → Ω' compatible with δ and ν.

Theorem 1:
- (a) An orientation theory exists, e.g. via local homology H_m(V, V∖x).
- (b) There is at most one morphism between two theories, and any morphism is an isomorphism (rigidity, since stalks are 2-element torsors pinned down by ν through iterated Stokes maps).
- (c) For N ≠ 4 any two theories are isomorphic.

The next page explains the role of N ≠ 4. Locally constant sheaves on the big site 𝒱_m are equivalent to Π(m)-sets, where Π(m) is the group completion of the discrete monoid of continuous injective self-maps of R^m. In other words, π₁ of the big topos of m-manifolds is Π(m). The Brouwer degree gives Π(m) → μ₂, which is an isomorphism iff every degree +1 homeomorphism of R^m is stable; Kirby's theorem supplies this for m ≠ 4. The problem served is a characterisation of 'orientation' purely by sheaf-theoretic and Stokes-type axioms, as a universal object up to unique isomorphism, in Grothendieck's style.
errors: In (c)(ii) the formula δ_V(ω) = ω̄|∂U should read δ_U(ω). This is an abuse of notation, harmless by naturality of δ.

Not an error in 1981, but now outdated: the restriction N ≠ 4 in Theorem 1(c) and the Corollary is unnecessary. Quinn (1982, 'Ends of maps III') proved the 4-dimensional annulus/stable homeomorphism theorem. The low dimensions were already classical (Radó, Moise, Brown–Gluck), and Kirby's [2] properly covers only m ≥ 5. So deg_m : Π(m) → μ₂ is an isomorphism for all m, and orientation theories are unique in every dimension.

The Proposition's proof is only sketched. It needs Theorem 2 (separation implies local constancy) plus the iterated Stokes isomorphism down to a point. The note does not show how axioms (a)–(c) alone fix the stalk cardinality at 2 in each dimension ≤ N. It is plausible, but it relies on the thesis [3].

ideas.what: Axiomatic characterisation of orientations as a separated sheaf on the site of manifolds with open embeddings, with a Stokes (boundary-induction) local isomorphism, a normalisation at the point, and a sign axiom for cutting along hypersurfaces; existence and rigidity (unique isomorphism) of such theories
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic/universal characterisation of the orientation double cover (orientation local system) via sheaves on Mfd_n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Wanderley (thesis Montpellier 1980, CRAS 1981), presumably on Grothendieck's suggestion
ideas.where_published: M. Wanderley, CRAS 292 (1981) 213–215; thèse de 3e cycle Montpellier 1980

ideas.what: Separation axiom: coincidence loci of sections are clopen (Hausdorff étalé space), equivalent to local constancy on the big site
ideas.modern_name: Separated (Hausdorff) sheaf / locally constant sheaf on Mfd_m
ideas.where_published: CRAS note (this page and the next)

ideas.what: Stokes map as an isomorphism of étalé spaces between germs of orientations along ∂V and orientations of ∂V; anti-commutativity sign axiom
ideas.modern_name: Boundary orientation convention (outward normal first), collar compatibility

ideas.what: Uniqueness of orientation theory reduced to the stable homeomorphism property of R^m via the group completion Π(m) of Mon(R^m) (π₁ of the big topos of m-manifolds)
ideas.modern_name: π₀ of the topological structure group Top(m) ≅ Z/2 / stable homeomorphism conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brown–Gluck (stable homeomorphisms), Kirby 1969, Quinn 1982 (dim 4); the topos formulation is due to Wanderley

missed.claim: The dimension-4 exception in Theorem 1(c) can be removed using Quinn's 1982 proof of the 4-dimensional stable homeomorphism/annulus theorem. Any two orientation theories are then uniquely isomorphic in all dimensions, and Π(m) ≅ μ₂ for every m. The note predates this and nobody seems to have recorded the update.
missed.quote: (c) Si N≠4 il existe un (unique) isomorphisme entre deux théories de l'orientation des variétés topologiques en dimension ≦ N.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It completes the axiomatic uniqueness statement. It also yields a clean statement: the fundamental group of the big topos of topological m-manifolds with open embeddings is Z/2 for all m.

missed.claim: Wanderley's framework (sheaves on the site of m-manifolds with open embeddings; locally constant ones equivalent to sets with an action of the group completion of the embedding monoid of R^m) is a discrete, 1-categorical precursor of the Ayala–Francis/Lurie picture. There, locally constant (homotopy) sheaves on Mfd_m correspond to spaces with an action of Emb(R^m, R^m) ≃ Top(m). That later literature does not cite this work.
missed.quote: Le foncteur Ω→Ω(R^m) : L.C.(𝒱_m)→Π(m)-Ens est une équivalence de catégories (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an elementary, set-level instance of the tangential-structure classification used in factorization homology. It also poses a concrete question: compute the group completion of the discrete monoid Mon(R^m), and compare it with π₀ Top(m).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a published CRAS note by a Grothendieck student, not an unpublished Grothendieck text. The mathematics is a neat axiomatics of orientation and is in print. Mild interest lies in its little-known topos-theoretic link to stable homeomorphisms, and in the fact that the N≠4 caveat is now obsolete.
transcription_corrections: The transcription of this page is essentially accurate. In axiom (d) the image indeed reads 𝒱_{≤N} (no bullet), while the Proposition reads 𝒱•_{≤N}.
The display Ω•_V | ∂V → Ω_{∂V} is printed with an isomorphism arrow (⥲); rendering it as \xrightarrow{\sim} is fine.
Previous page: 'orientation unduite' should read 'orientation induite'.
